# Session Handoff System for pi

Persistent project memory across chat sessions: a living `PROJECT.md` per repo + timestamped handoff checkpoints, so a fresh session resumes with minimal re-reading.

## Components

| Piece | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `project-md` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/project-md/SKILL.md` | Create `PROJECT.md`; log ADRs with strike-through history |
| `handoff-create` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/handoff-create/SKILL.md` | Write a session checkpoint to `handoffs/` |
| `handoff-resume` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/handoff-resume/SKILL.md` | Restore context in a new chat from PROJECT.md + one checkpoint |
| Global rule | `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` | Every session reads/follows `PROJECT.md` when present |
| Data (per repo) | `<repo>/PROJECT.md`, `<repo>/handoffs/*.md` | Committable project memory |

## Lifecycle

```
session start ─► PROJECT.md auto-read (AGENTS.md rule)
      │
work ──────────► decision made/reversed? ─► project-md: ~~strike~~ + dated ADR entry
      │
wrap up ───────► handoff-create ─► handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM_<lane>_<slug>.md
      │
new chat ──────► handoff-resume ─► reads PROJECT.md + 1 checkpoint ─► work continues
```

## File formats

### PROJECT.md (repo root, ≤60 lines, fixed section names)


[190 more lines in file. Use offset=31 to continue.]

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Resume, no `PROJECT.md` | Says so, continues from checkpoints if any exist |
| `handoffs/` missing/empty | Says so, works from `PROJECT.md` alone — no error |
| ADR requested, no `PROJECT.md` | Asks whether to initialize (no silent create, no silent skip) |
| Not a git repo | Lane omitted from filename and frontmatter; lane-less checkpoints carry forward among themselves |
| Same-minute collision | `-2`, `-3` suffix |
| Multiple lanes, no fragment | Lists lanes, asks which |
| quota-axi < 10% (FirstMate) | Handoff still written, with `## Note: quota low, session ended early` |
| Multiple worktrees on same repo | `project-md` goes append-only (no strikethrough); git merge reconciles |

## Why it's token-efficient

- **Progressive disclosure**: only skill descriptions sit in the system prompt; full SKILL.md loads on trigger.
- **Reference, don't duplicate**: checkpoints cite `PROJECT.md §` sections; `PROJECT.md` never restates checkpoint detail.
- **Resume reads 2 files** by default, not the checkpoint history.
- **Create reads 0 files**: written from session context (plus the carry-forward peek at one previous checkpoint).
- **Hard caps**: ≤10 bullets/section, no empty-section stubs, no prose paragraphs, PROJECT.md ≤60 lines with a stable-size top and append-only log.

## Ops

- **After editing any SKILL.md or AGENTS.md: restart pi** — skills and context files load at startup.
- Skill auto-triggering is best-effort; if the model doesn't load the skill, say "use the handoff-create skill" or run `/skill:handoff-create`.
- Never install the same skill name in two locations — pi keeps the first found and shadows the rest.
- Commit `PROJECT.md` and `handoffs/` for team-visible history, or gitignore `handoffs/` if checkpoints are private.
- FirstMate/Treehouse-only behaviors: worktree-derived lanes, quota-axi check, crewmate hand-back trigger, multi-worktree append-only mode. Elsewhere lane falls back to `git branch --show-current` and everything else is identical.

## FirstMate workspace addendum

The global skills work as-is in a FirstMate coordinator workspace; degradation rules cover whatever is missing. Once that workspace exists (per `FirstMate-Herdr-Pi_setup.md`), two one-time steps complete the integration:

1. **Project-level AGENTS.md** — the generic PROJECT.md convention is already covered by the global file, so the workspace repo's own `AGENTS.md` needs only the FirstMate delta:

2. **Environment checks** (once, in the coordinator session):

content.thinking:
I now have everything I need. Let me summarize the research findings and write the plan.

## Research findings

**Does bare pi have automatic per-task-type model/effort routing? No.** Confirmed:
- No routing config file in bare pi (all "routing" hits are OpenRouter/provider-level, tool routing, keybindings).
- FirstMate's routing table was its own extension layer.

**What bare pi DOES have:**

1. **Manual switching (built-in)**:
   - `/model` picker (Ctrl+S saves startup default), `/thinking` picker (Ctrl+S saves default)
   - Ctrl+P cycles `enabledModels` patterns — and patterns can pin thinking levels: `--models "kimi-k3:high,glm-5.2:medium"` style (`provider/id:level` syntax from `--model` flag; scoped models support `thinkingLevel` per pattern per the extensions doc on `ctx.scopedModels`)
   - CLI: `--model provider/id:high`, `--thinking high`, `--models` patterns
   - Settings: `defaultModel`, `defaultThinkingLevel`, `modelThinkingLevels` (per-model startup thinking)

2. **Extension API — full programmatic control**:
   - `pi.setModel(model)`, `pi.setThinkingLevel(level)` (session-scoped, restored on resume)
   - `input` event: fires on raw user input BEFORE skill/template expansion — can see `/skill:handoff-create` before expansion! Can transform/handle/continue.
   - `before_agent_start`: sees the final prompt + loaded skills (`event.systemPromptOptions.skills`) — can switch model/effort based on what skill got loaded!
   - `registerCommand`, `registerShortcut`, footer widgets.
   - Events `model_select`, `thinking_level_select` for UI sync.

3. **Two example extensions that are 80% of the solution**:
   - `preset.ts`: named presets (provider, model, thinkingLevel, tools, instructions) from `~/.pi/agent/presets.json` + project `.pi/presets.json`; activate via `--preset` flag, `/preset` command, Ctrl+Shift+U cycling. This IS phase profiles — plan/implement example config literally included in the file header.
   - `plan-mode/`: read-only planning mode with tool restriction, `/plan` command + Ctrl+Alt+P toggle, plan-step extraction and execution tracking.

So the answer to the user's question: **bare pi has no automatic routing, but it has (a) solid manual mechanisms and (b) an extension API with the exact hooks needed to build automatic or one-keystroke routing — including an official example (`preset.ts`) that already implements model+effort profiles.**

## The plan (tiered)

**Tier 0 — zero build, manual (start today)**:
- Configure `enabledModels` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` with thinking-pinned patterns mapping to the three tiers: e.g. `["kimi-k3:high", "glm-5.3:high", "glm-5.2:medium"]` (exact IDs from their models-store.json catalogue).
- Ctrl+P cycles tiers; `/model`+`/thinking` for fine control.
- Skill-level soft routing already exists: handoff-create says "lowest adequate effort" (model follows instruction if it can... no — the skill can't change its own effort. The instruction is for the harness IF it exposes per-call routing. In bare pi, the skill text can't switch the model. So soft routing only works via the human or an extension).

**Tier 1 — preset extension (small, recommended)**: adopt/adapt `preset.ts`:
- `~/.pi/agent/presets.json` with three profiles: `plan` (Kimi K3/GLM 5.3, high), `execute` (GLM 5.2, medium), `review` (Kimi K3/GLM 5.3, high + adversarial instructions).
- Switch via `/preset plan` or Ctrl+Shift+U. One keystroke at phase boundary.
- Optional: per-preset `instructions` bake in phase behavior (read-only plan mode, adversarial review stance).
- Optionally combine with plan-mode's tool restriction for the plan preset.

**Tier 2 — auto-routing hooks (optional, later)**: small extension that listens to `input`/`before_agent_start` and auto-switches:
- `/skill:handoff-create` or `/skill:handoff-resume` detected in `input` → ensure execution tier (or lowest effort) before expansion.
- `before_agent_start` → if loaded skills include project-md ADR-ish work... harder to detect reliably. Better triggers: explicit commands.
- Risk: misclassification → the reviewer's warning (weak model on hard task burns more than strong model). Mitigation: auto-route ONLY the unambiguous cheap cases (handoff skills), leave plan/review/execute to manual preset switching.

**Validation protocol (from the reviewer, adopted)**: before committing to GLM 5.2 for execution, A/B 5-10 real recent execution tasks: GLM 5.2@medium vs GLM 5.3@default; measure first-pass correctness + retry count, not token cost. If 5.2 fails >rarely, use 5.3@medium instead (Kun's actual day-to-day move: same model, dialed-down reasoning).

Also worth noting: `modelThinkingLevels` setting gives per-model default thinking — so selecting GLM 5.2 can auto-start at medium without a separate /thinking step. That makes even Tier 0 nearly one-action.

Structure of my answer:
1. Direct answer to the scope question: no automatic routing in bare pi; manual + extension hooks; FirstMate's was its own layer.
2. What exists (table: mechanism → what it gives).
3. The two example extensions that are 80% of the build.
4. Plan: Tier 0 / Tier 1 / Tier 2 + validation protocol + how it maps to the skills we built.
5. Note on the skills: handoff-create's "lowest adequate effort" line is inert in bare pi without an extension — Tier 2's auto-route on `/skill:handoff-*` would activate it.

Keep it tight. This is a plan-only deliverable.

**No automatic per-task routing exists in bare pi.** Confirmed — every "routing" hit in the docs is provider-level (OpenRouter/Vercel gateway), tool routing, or keybindings. Kun's routing table was FirstMate's own extension layer, not a pi feature. But the building blocks are all there:

| Mechanism | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `/model`, `/thinking` pickers | Manual switch; Ctrl+S saves startup defaults |
| `modelThinkingLevels` setting | **Per-model** default thinking level — selecting GLM 5.2 can auto-start at `medium`, no separate `/thinking` step |
| `enabledModels` + Ctrl+P | Cycle a curated model list; patterns can pin effort (`glm-5.2:medium`) |
| CLI | `--model kimi-k3:high`, `--preset plan` at launch |
| Extension API | `pi.setModel()` + `pi.setThinkingLevel()` (session-scoped, survive resume), plus the two hooks that matter: **`input`** (sees raw text *before* skill expansion — can spot `/skill:handoff-create`) and **`before_agent_start`** (sees the final prompt + which skills loaded) |

**Two official example extensions are ~80% of the solution already:**
- `examples/extensions/preset.ts` — named presets (provider, model, thinkingLevel, tools, *system-prompt instructions*) from `~/.pi/agent/presets.json`, switched via `/preset <name>` or Ctrl+Shift+U. Its header example is literally a `plan`/`implement` pair.
- `examples/extensions/plan-mode/` — read-only planning mode (tool restriction, `/plan` toggle, plan-step tracking).

## Plan (tiered, each tier standalone)

**Tier 0 — zero build, do today.** Add `enabledModels` with effort-pinned patterns to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (e.g. `["kimi-k3:high", "glm-5.3:high", "glm-5.2:medium"]` — exact IDs from your `models-store.json`), plus `modelThinkingLevels` so 5.2 defaults to medium. Phase switch = Ctrl+P. Cost: one settings edit. Friction: you are the router.

**Tier 1 — preset extension (recommended).** Adopt `preset.ts` (copy example → `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`), write three profiles in `presets.json`:
- `plan` → Kimi K3 or GLM 5.3, `high`, optionally read-only tools (borrow plan-mode's restriction)
- `execute` → GLM 5.2, `medium`
- `review` → K3/5.3, `high` + adversarial-review instructions baked into the preset's `instructions` field (your third tier, the reviewer's "No Mistakes" row)

# Session Handoff System for pi

Persistent project memory across chat sessions: a living `PROJECT.md` per repo + timestamped handoff checkpoints, so a fresh session resumes with minimal re-reading.

## Components

| Piece | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `project-md` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/project-md/SKILL.md` | Create `PROJECT.md`; log ADRs with strike-through history; wire repo `AGENTS.md` auto-read on init |
| `handoff-create` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/handoff-create/SKILL.md` | Write a session checkpoint to `handoffs/` |
| `handoff-resume` skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/handoff-resume/SKILL.md` | Restore context in a new chat from PROJECT.md + one checkpoint |
| Global rule | `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` | Git commit discipline — kebab-case feature branches, never push; branch name = handoff lane |
| Data (per repo) | `<repo>/PROJECT.md`, `<repo>/handoffs/*.md` | Committable project memory |

## Lifecycle

```
work ──────────► decision made/reversed? ─► project-md: ~~strike~~ + dated ADR entry
      │
feature done ──► commit on kebab-case branch (global rule; branch name = lane)
      │
wrap up ───────► handoff-create ─► handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM_<lane>_<slug>.md
      │
new chat ──────► handoff-resume ─► reads PROJECT.md + 1 checkpoint ─► work continues
```

## Git commit discipline (global rule)

`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` applies to every repo: after a significant, working change (never mid-task/WIP), the agent commits on a kebab-case feature branch — never directly on `main`/`master`, never `git push` (pushing is manual, user-only).

Free integration: the branch name becomes the next handoff's **lane** automatically (`handoff-create` reads `git branch --show-current`), and kebab-case names make the filename-sanitize step a no-op.

## File formats

### PROJECT.md (repo root, ≤60 lines, fixed section names)

```markdown
# PROJECT.md

## Goal
## Architecture
## Structure
## Conventions
## ADR Log
### YYYY-MM-DD — <decision title>
```

Update rules: never delete; superseded text gets `~~strikethrough~~ → replacement (ADR <date>)`; ADR entries are dated, ≤3 lines, append-only. Sections are never renamed/reordered — checkpoints reference them as `PROJECT.md § <section>`.

### Handoff checkpoint
